\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نردبان} (nardebân)}{نردبان (nardebân)}]{\fa{نردبان} (nardebân) — a ladder}

\label{lesson:FA-C112-nardeban}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bucket, then the Persian for a rope.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نردبان}}
\textbf{\fa{نردبان}} — \emph{nardebân} — \textquotedblleft{}a ladder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nardebân} is a native Persian word, inherited rather than borrowed; it is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{nardubān}, \textquotedblleft{}ladder\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\fa{صندوق}} — \emph{sanduq} — \textquotedblleft{}a chest, a box\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{چمدان} (chamedân)}{چمدان (chamedân)}]{\fa{چمدان} (chamedân) — a suitcase}

\label{lesson:FA-C112-chamedan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a ladder, then the Persian for a chest.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{چمدان}}
\textbf{\fa{چمدان}} — \emph{chamedân} — \textquotedblleft{}a suitcase\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{chamedân} is usually explained as the Persian \emph{jâmedân}, \textquotedblleft{}clothes-holder\textquotedblright{} (\emph{jâme}, \textquotedblleft{}garment\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-dân}, \textquotedblleft{}container\textquotedblright{}), which went into Russian as \emph{chemodan} and was borrowed back in that shape.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کوله} \fa{پشتی} (kuleposhti)}{کوله پشتی (kuleposhti)}]{\fa{کوله} \fa{پشتی} (kuleposhti) — a backpack}

\label{lesson:FA-C112-kuleposhti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a chest, then the Persian for a suitcase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کوله} \fa{پشتی}}
\textbf{\fa{کوله} \fa{پشتی}} — \emph{kuleposhti} — \textquotedblleft{}a backpack\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kuleposhti} is built from \emph{kule}, \textquotedblleft{}load\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{posht}, \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-i}: a load for the back. \emph{posht} is inherited, usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{pušt}.
\end{cousinweb}
